plan.title: Per-sample hallmark GSVA in UC inflamed colon
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark heatmap that shows which pathways separate ulcerative colitis inflamed colon from control. The input is a raw Salmon gene-level count matrix (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples) with a 12-row metadata table carrying condition (6 UC inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch). Sample-level gene set scoring needs a variance-stabilised, library-size-corrected expression matrix, not raw counts — so T1S1 normalises with DESeq2 VST (appropriate at n=12 and robust to the one flagged outlier), filters low-count genes, resolves duplicate gene symbols, and runs unsupervised QC (library sizes, PCA, sample correlation) with explicit attention to sample_01, whose library size is ~4x below the median. Because size-factor normalisation plus VST handles depth differences, sample_01 is retained by default and flagged, not dropped — but the QC output must state whether it is an expression-space outlier so downstream results can be read accordingly.

T1S2 computes the per-sample scores themselves: GSVA on the VST matrix against the 50 human MSigDB hallmark sets (staged at /mnt/refs as h.all symbols GMT, HGNC symbols matching the counts' first column), producing a 50 x 12 sample-by-pathway activity matrix — the direct answer to 'a pathway activity score for every sample'. ssGSEA is added as a second, differently-parameterised scoring method so that the reported separation is not an artefact of one estimator. T1S3 does the statistics and the figure: a moderated t-test (limma) on the hallmark score matrix with BH correction to rank pathways by UC-inflamed vs control separation, then the requested heatmap of hallmark activity across all 12 samples (z-scored per pathway, samples annotated by condition), plus a version restricted to the significantly separating pathways. Ranking on the same 12 samples that defined the contrast means the heatmap's apparent separation is descriptive, not a validated classifier — the step must say so. T1S4 grounds the pathway-level result in gene-level differential expression (DESeq2 Wald on raw counts) so that a hallmark called as separating can be checked against the actual genes driving it, which is the standard guard against a score-level artefact.
